summary: EXPERIMENT RESULT (client question: 'did you try the snippet without any variant-id attribute at all?') = ANSWER (a) SUCCESS. With REACT_APP_TINT_VARIANT_ID empty and Fit.jsx rendering variant-id={TINT_VARIANT_ID || undefined}, React omits the attribute entirely: document.querySelector('tint-vto').getAttribute('variant-id') === null and hasAttribute('variant-id') === false (only publishable-key + style + dev x-* attrs present). The widget then posts to https://api.tintvto.com/api/v1/public/resolve with the variantId key COMPLETELY ABSENT from the JSON body: {"idempotencyKey":"3823b1d4-...","includeCatalogPreload":true,"locale":"en","publishableKey":"pk_live_IYyrrt3UVJlY4ogS1rsQkOpb5hPMSyodJB9dhszNeKQ"} -- and the response is HTTP 200 with a full catalog payload (catalog.baseUrl=https://api.tintvto.com/api/v1/public/catalog, delivery='api', preload.products with prd_5003e82ff9853b42e29212b9ac748870 'Alexander McQueen', externalId/sku 'XenonPL_00000000001', tryOn.kind='3d', plus Fendi / Gucci / Saint Laurent SL 347/364/378/386 etc.). The 404 product_not_found from iteration_25 is GONE. Only ONE resolve call is made (no retry loop). The vendor modal now renders the real default catalog picker (grid of ~16+ frame thumbnails) next to the live try-on canvas, and product selection WORKS: clicking the first thumbnail marked it 'Applied' and updated the vendor panel to 'Applied products (1) - Alexander McQueen'. The try-on canvas shows the headless browser's synthetic green camera frame with a rendered WebAR mesh overlay (expected in a headless test container without a real webcam/face; not a defect). Console: only 'info: [tint-vto] Banuba WebAR SDK version: 1.18.4' plus benign WebGL 'GPU stall due to ReadPixels' perf warnings and the pre-existing /hero/xoexam-arm.webp preload warning. ZERO 'Missing client token' sdkError, ZERO pageerrors, ZERO React/app console errors -> the code change (variant-id -> undefined) introduced no new errors. Vendor modal closes via its own x at page.mouse.click(1896,24) and the page stays fully interactive (fit-tab-core clicked successfully after close). Verified across two independent runs, identical results. Frontend was restarted to pick up the new empty .env value.
action_items: Report to the client: YES - omitting the variant-id attribute entirely works. resolve returns 200 with a client token + default catalog; the picker and try-on load, and product selection applies. Keep REACT_APP_TINT_VARIANT_ID empty (or supply a REAL variant-id) - never the 'MERCHANT_VARIANT_ID' placeholder, which is what caused 404 product_not_found.

Guard the empty-string case permanently: keep variant-id={TINT_VARIANT_ID || undefined} and consider trimming (TINT_VARIANT_ID?.trim() || undefined) so a whitespace-only env value cannot reintroduce an empty attribute.

Optional (carry-over from iteration_24/25, no longer blocking): data-testid='vto-error-message' is still unreachable because tint-vto.open() always resolves; if a vendor failure watchdog is still wanted, hook the resolve response instead of racing open().
critical_code_review_comments: Confirmed at DOM level that React omits boolean-absent props correctly for custom elements when the value is undefined - the fix behaves exactly as intended (attribute absent, not empty string).

The vendor treats an absent variantId as 'open in default catalog mode', while an empty-string or bogus variantId is treated as a lookup and 404s. Never pass a placeholder/empty string through to the attribute.

success_rate.frontend: 100% - integration and vendor widget end-to-end both working: DOM attribute omitted, resolve 200 + catalog, picker interactive, product apply works, modal close + post-close interactivity OK, no new console/runtime errors

context_for_next_testing_agent: The Tint/Banuba VTO is now FULLY WORKING on the preview host with NO variant-id attribute (REACT_APP_TINT_VARIANT_ID empty). Do not re-report origin_denied (fixed, iteration_25) or product_not_found (resolved by omitting the attribute, iteration_26). Repro: /xofit-frame-fitting -> dismiss cookie banner (button:has-text('Accept')) -> click [data-testid=fit-tab-frame] -> scroll to + click [data-testid=vto-trigger-button] -> catalog grid appears in the vendor modal within ~10s. Modal is a full-viewport overlay that blocks Playwright element clicks; use page.mouse.click for in-modal interaction (first product thumb ~ (531,253) at 1920x1080) and page.mouse.click(1896,24) to close. Escape does not close it. Green canvas = headless synthetic camera, not a bug.
rca_of_the_issue: Tint's /api/v1/public/resolve has two modes. When variantId is present it performs a product lookup and returns 404 product_not_found for an unknown/placeholder value (iteration_25 with 'MERCHANT_VARIANT_ID'). When the variantId key is absent from the request body entirely, the endpoint falls back to publishable-key-scoped default catalog mode and returns 200 with the merchant catalog preload plus the client token needed by the Banuba WebAR SDK. Because React only omits an attribute when the prop is undefined (an empty string still renders variant-id=""), the fix variant-id={TINT_VARIANT_ID || undefined} is exactly what unlocked the 200.
